title: Dhamaal 4 Just Dropped Four Posters. There Are Crocodiles, Pirates, and Arshad Warsi Buried in Sand.
excerpt: The gang's biggest treasure hunt yet arrives July 10 — preponed by a week because even Indra Kumar knows better than to open against Christopher Nolan.
body:
Dhamaal 4 Just Dropped Four Posters. There Are Crocodiles, Pirates, and Arshad Warsi Buried in Sand.

There are franchise posters, and then there are Dhamaal posters — the kind where you look at them and think, "This is either going to be magnificent or an absolute catastrophe, and honestly either outcome sounds fun."

Dhamaal 4 unveiled four character posters on June 9, and the franchise's signature unhinged energy is immediately apparent. Ajay Devgn and Sanjay Mishra are dangling from a rock face, desperately trying not to become lunch for a pack of crocodiles below. Devgn captioned it himself on Instagram: "Inn dono ka hai ek hi goal, to get their hands on gold." The tagline reads: "The Adventure Awaits!"

The second poster puts Riteish Deshmukh in full Indiana Jones mode — suspended mid-air in a brown jacket and red bandana, tangled in green vines, with a monkey perched on a nearby branch looking distinctly unimpressed by the whole situation. Anjali Anand appears equally alarmed beside him. "HUNT BEGINS SOON!" reads the tagline, confirming what the posters collectively suggest: a treasure hunt narrative driving the chaos this time around.

Then there's the beach poster, and it's the one that tells you exactly what kind of film this is. Arshad Warsi, Jaaved Jaaferi, and Sanjeeda Shaikh are buried neck-deep in sand while crabs scuttle menacingly around their heads. A partially visible treasure map peeks out from the foreground. The tagline: "CHASE STARTS NOW!" If you've ever seen an Arshad Warsi reaction face, you already know what his expression looks like, and it's perfect.

The fourth poster introduces Ravi Kishan as what appears to be the film's antagonist — a full-blown pirate, complete with henchmen played by Vijay Patkar and Upendra Limaye. It's the kind of casting choice that only the Dhamaal franchise would attempt with a straight face.

Directed by Indra Kumar, who's helmed every entry since the 2007 original, the sequel also adds Esha Gupta to what is already one of Bollywood's most deliberately overstuffed ensemble casts.

Why July 10 and Not July 17

Here's the behind-the-scenes move that trade watchers are talking about. The film was originally slated for July 17, but the makers quietly moved it a week earlier. The reason is one name: Christopher Nolan. His epic The Odyssey opens worldwide on July 17 and is already selling out IMAX screens across India — with advance booking prices ranging from ₹370 in Delhi to a genuinely wild ₹3,000 in Pune.

No Bollywood producer in their right mind wants to share opening-week screens with Nolan at peak demand, and the Dhamaal team made the pragmatic call. The revised date actually works in the film's favour: a clean opening week with no Hollywood heavyweight hogging the multiplexes gives it the best chance to build word-of-mouth — which, for a comedy franchise that has always been a slow burn rather than a day-one spectacle, is everything.

The Franchise Track Record

For the uninitiated: the original Dhamaal (2007) became a cult comedy classic, the kind of film that plays on TV loops during long weekends and nobody changes the channel. Double Dhamaal (2011) divided audiences but made its money. Total Dhamaal (2019) crossed ₹150 crore at the domestic box office, proving the franchise still had serious commercial legs seven years after the previous instalment.

The formula hasn't fundamentally changed — take a group of loveable idiots, put them in increasingly absurd situations, and let the chaos write itself. What's new is the adventure scale: jungles, beaches, pirates, treasure maps. It's leaning into It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World territory with a distinctly desi twist.

For the Diaspora

The Dhamaal films have always been comfort cinema for NRI audiences — the kind of no-stakes, leave-your-brain-at-the-door comedy that works at family gatherings, holiday watch parties, and lazy weekend streams. The fourth instalment promises to be even more visually spectacular while keeping the core appeal intact. For Indians abroad, this film offers a chance to reconnect with the humor and chaos of Bollywood, which often serves as a bridge to their cultural roots. Many NRIs might anticipate watching this film as a way to share a laugh with family back home, or to introduce their children to a beloved Indian comedy franchise, fostering a shared cultural experience across generations. The anticipation around this release may also influence remittance patterns, as families plan movie nights and gatherings around the film's release. Moreover, the film's comedic elements and relatable characters can spark conversations among diaspora communities, reinforcing their ties to Indian culture and traditions.

As the excitement builds, social media is already having fun with the posters. Fans are noting the absence of Sanjay Dutt and Madhuri Dixit from the franchise, which has led to speculation about potential cameos or future projects.
